slides.title: BIOGLOW Season Lesson
slides.body: Today we are learning what the 2026-2027 FIRST LEGO League BIOGLOW season is about, what topics our team should start studying, and how we can make smart predictions about the Innovation Project prompt before the full challenge is released.

slides.title: What We Know Officially
slides.body: BIOGLOW is the 2026-2027 FIRST LEGO League season. FIRST says teams will explore the vibrancy of the world's ecosystems, biodiversity, and the connection between nature, technology, and innovation. Full Challenge details release on August 4, 2026.

slides.title: Big Idea: Ecosystems
slides.body: An ecosystem is a community of living things and the nonliving parts of their environment. That includes plants, animals, fungi, bacteria, soil, water, air, light, temperature, and human activity. In BIOGLOW, we should think in systems: when one part changes, other parts can change too.

slides.title: Big Idea: Biodiversity
slides.body: Biodiversity means the variety of life in an area. It can mean many different species, genetic variety within a species, and different habitats working together. Healthy biodiversity can make ecosystems stronger, more balanced, and more able to recover after stress.

slides.title: Why BIOGLOW Matters
slides.body: Ecosystems affect food, clean water, clean air, medicine, climate, recreation, and neighborhood health. Problems in ecosystems are not only animal problems or plant problems. They are human problems too. That is why this theme is a strong Innovation Project theme.

slides.title: Focus Topic 1: Local Ecosystems
slides.body: Start close to home. Study parks, street trees, school gardens, rivers, ponds, coastal areas, vacant lots, and neighborhood wildlife. A local problem is easier to observe, test, photograph, interview people about, and improve.

slides.title: Focus Topic 2: Habitats
slides.body: A habitat is the place where an organism gets what it needs to live. Good research questions: What species live here? What do they need? What is missing? What barriers, dangers, or changes make survival harder?

slides.title: Focus Topic 3: Human Impact
slides.body: Look for ways human choices affect ecosystems: trash, light pollution, noise, construction, invasive species, pesticides, water pollution, heat, flooding, and habitat loss. Strong projects usually connect a real problem to a real group of people who can use the solution.

slides.title: Focus Topic 4: Balance
slides.body: Ecosystems depend on balance. Predators, pollinators, decomposers, plants, water, sunlight, and nutrients all interact. If one connection breaks, the system can shift. Our team should practice drawing food webs and cause-effect chains.

slides.title: Focus Topic 5: Nature + Technology
slides.body: BIOGLOW is not only about nature. It is about nature, technology, and innovation. Useful technology topics include sensors, cameras, environmental data, mapping, robotics, AI, apps, citizen science, bio-inspired design, and tools that help people notice ecosystem changes.

slides.title: Pattern: SUBMERGED
slides.body: In 2024-2025, SUBMERGED focused on the ocean. Teams explored ocean layers and used STEM and creativity to solve problems faced by ocean explorers. Pattern: FIRST chose a real-world field, asked students to learn from experts, then create useful solutions.

slides.title: Pattern: UNEARTHED
slides.body: In 2025-2026, UNEARTHED focused on archaeology. Teams learned about real challenges archaeologists face and connected science, technology, history, and communities. Pattern: the Innovation Project is usually not broad like 'make archaeology better.' It asks teams to find one specific problem and design one specific solution.

slides.title: What the Last Two Years Suggest
slides.body: SUBMERGED and UNEARTHED both pointed teams toward a theme, but the project work came from choosing a focused problem inside that theme. For BIOGLOW, we should expect the project to involve ecosystems or biodiversity, but our best preparation is learning enough to choose a real, narrow, testable problem.

slides.title: Important: This Is a Prediction
slides.body: The official BIOGLOW Innovation Project prompt is not released yet. The next slides are our forecast based on official BIOGLOW wording and the pattern from recent FLL seasons. Once the challenge releases, we will update our project plan to match the real prompt.

slides.title: Predicted Innovation Prompt
slides.body: Our best prediction: Identify a problem that affects biodiversity, ecosystem health, or the balance between humans and nature. Research who is affected, learn from experts, design an innovative solution that helps protect, restore, monitor, or improve an ecosystem, then share and improve your solution.

slides.title: Possible Project Areas
slides.body:
Possible areas to research:

Pollinator habitats
Street tree health
Urban heat and plants
Wetlands and flooding
Water quality
Invasive species
Bird-safe buildings
Light pollution
Composting and soil health
Schoolyard biodiversity
Park trash and wildlife
Monitoring local species

slides.title: What Makes a Strong BIOGLOW Project?
slides.body: A strong project has a specific user, specific place, specific problem, and specific test. Weak: 'Save animals.' Strong: 'Help our school reduce nighttime light near windows so migrating birds are safer.' Weak: 'Plant more trees.' Strong: 'Help homeowners choose native plants that support pollinators in small front yards.'

slides.title: Research Questions to Start Now
slides.body:
Ask:

What ecosystem problem can we observe locally?
Which species, people, or places are affected?
What already exists to solve it?
Why are current solutions not enough?
Who can we interview?
What small prototype could we test in two weeks?

slides.title: How This Connects to Robot Game
slides.body: We do not know the exact missions yet, but BIOGLOW missions will likely connect to ecosystems, habitats, biodiversity, or human-nature balance. Start preparing robot skills that always matter: accurate driving, line following, attachment alignment, lift mechanisms, pushing/pulling, collecting, delivering, and fast resets.

slides.title: Team Action Plan
slides.body:
Before kickoff, each team should build a BIOGLOW idea bank:

1. List 10 local ecosystem problems.
2. Pick 3 that are observable.
3. Find one expert or community contact for each.
4. Sketch one possible solution.
5. Save photos, sources, and notes in the engineering notebook.
